manifesto_l2.current: An edge is never given — it is forged.
manifesto_l2.A: Every edge is paid for — first by the metal.
manifesto_l2.B: The edge decides before the hand does.
manifesto_l2.C: What the whetstone takes, the edge keeps.

inscription.current: You say what others soften — and pay, quietly, for being the one who did.
inscription.A: You say what others soften — and carry alone what the saying costs.
inscription.B: You finish reading a room before entering it — and are never quite inside.
inscription.C: You cut clean where others tear — and the clean cut is remembered as cold.

yourNature_desc.current: The most honest person in any room, often the most alone in it. Precision arrives before warmth does — people lean on the edge and rarely find what's behind it.
yourNature_desc.A: The most honest person in any room, often the most alone in it. Every truth you deliver is paid for privately — the room keeps the clarity, and you keep the bill.
yourNature_desc.B: You evaluate before you engage — the read completes before the conversation starts. What the room feels as edge is a verdict arriving early; what you feel is the distance it builds.
yourNature_desc.C: A blade in a room of cloth — everything near you falls into before and after. People borrow the edge for their knots, then flinch at it; the steel never gets to be soft.
